Slow-Smoked Baby Back Ribs

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 4-6Prep 30 min (plus 2-4 hours resting)Cook 4-6 hours

While the Feast of the Holy Innocents on December 28th is a day of solemn remembrance, historical traditions often included banquets to gather families and offer comfort during the winter season. These slow-smoked baby back ribs, tender and flavorful, provide a hearty centerpiece for such a Childermas banquet, offering warmth and sustenance amidst reflection and familial gathering.

Ingredients

  • 2 racks (about 4-5 lbs / 1.8-2.3 kg total) baby back pork ribs
  • For the Dry Rub:
  • 2 tablespoons (30g) light brown sugar, packed
  • 1 tablespoon (15g) smoked paprika
  • 1 tablespoon (15g) garlic powder
  • 1 tablespoon (15g) onion powder
  • 1 teaspoon (5g) black pepper
  • 1 teaspoon (5g) kosher salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5g) cayenne pepper (optional)
  • For the Mop/Spritz (optional):
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) apple cider vinegar
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) apple juice
  • Wood chips or chunks (hickory or apple wood recommended)

Method

  1. Prepare the ribs: Remove the thin membrane from the bone-side of each rack of ribs. To do this, slide a knife under the membrane at one end, lift it, then grasp it with a paper towel and pull it off. Pat the ribs dry with paper towels.
  2. Apply the dry rub: In a small bowl, combine all dry rub ingredients. Generously coat both sides of each rib rack with the rub, pressing it gently into the meat. Wrap the ribs tightly in plastic wrap or place them in a large sealed bag. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably 4 hours up to overnight, to allow the flavors to meld.
  3. Prepare the smoker: Preheat your smoker to a consistent temperature of 225°F (107°C). Add your chosen wood chips or chunks according to your smoker's instructions, ensuring a steady stream of thin, blue smoke.
  4. First smoke phase: Place the seasoned ribs directly on the smoker grates, bone-side down. Smoke for 2.5 to 3 hours, maintaining the smoker temperature. During this phase, you can spritz the ribs every hour with the apple cider vinegar and apple juice mixture if desired, to keep them moist.
  5. Wrap the ribs (the 'Texas Crutch'): Carefully remove the ribs from the smoker. Place each rack onto a large sheet of heavy-duty aluminum foil. If using the mop/spritz, lightly spray or brush the ribs one last time. Wrap each rack tightly in the foil, creating a sealed packet.
  6. Second smoke phase: Return the foil-wrapped ribs to the smoker. Continue to cook for another 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the ribs are very tender. They are done when the meat has pulled back from the ends of the bones and a toothpick can be easily inserted between the bones with little resistance.
  7. Finish the ribs (optional): If you desire a sticky glaze, carefully unwrap the ribs and brush them with your favorite BBQ sauce. Return the unwrapped ribs to the smoker for an additional 15-30 minutes to allow the sauce to set and caramelize.
  8. Rest and serve: Remove the ribs from the smoker. Let them rest, loosely tented with foil, for 10-15 minutes before slicing between the bones and serving hot.

Tips

  • For extra flavor and to help the rub adhere, spread a thin layer of yellow mustard on the ribs before applying the dry rub; it will cook off and not impart a mustard flavor.
  • The 'bend test' is a reliable indicator of doneness: pick up one end of a rack with tongs; if it bends significantly in the middle and the meat starts to crack, it's ready.
  • Serve these hearty ribs with classic winter sides like roasted root vegetables, creamy mashed potatoes, or a vibrant collard green slaw to complete your Childermas feast.
